title: (No AI) Microsoft says ‘people matter more than AI’ following safety concerns
author: Tom Warren
content:
![Vector illustration of the Microsoft logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/STK095_MICROSOFT_2_CVirginia_B.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Microsoft is publishing a 37-page "[humanist AI code of conduct](https://microsoft.ai/code-of-conduct/)" today, amid growing safety concerns over AI model progress. title: (No AI) Trump and Mike Johnson think the AI industry is overreacting
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![A photo of Donald Trump with an illustrated background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/09/STK466_ELECTION_2024_CVirginia_E.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Yesterday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a [lengthy open letter](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/994337/anthropic-ceo-slow-down-ai-development) saying it was time to "pace the frontier" and slow down AI development. OpenAI's [Sam Altman](https://x.com/sama/status/2098811563415150910) and [Elon Musk](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2098789109980332057) both agreed, publicly voicing their support on X. Even Alphabet's Demis Hassabis offered [tentative support](https://x.com/demishassabis/status/2098909516582490602) for Amodei's proposal.

Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson, however, seem to think the AI executives are being [overreactive](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/trump-defends-white-houses-light-touch-on-ai-regulation-c4ed2488) and fear that a pause could lead to China outpacing the US in the AI race. According to the _[Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/cae60732-f929-4735-a627-db8c14e7c7ed)_, Trump said "Look, we're leading China in AI … and, frankly, I want to keep it that way, because whoever wins AI, wins."
